question: A cuboid has dimensions 10 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm. If the largest possible cube is cut from one of the corners of the cuboid, what is the total surface area of the remaining portion?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a rectangular block or cube is cut from the corner of a cuboid, the net change in its total surface area is zero.

This is because the area of the 3 faces removed is exactly equal to the area of the 3 new inner faces created.

New TSA = Original TSA of the cuboid = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)

New TSA = 2 × (10 × 8 + 8 × 6 + 6 × 10) = 2 × (80 + 48 + 60)

New TSA = 2 × 188 = 376 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 376 cm².**

 Removed Cube
 (3 faces exposed)

 Surface Area Lost = Surface Area Created

**Given:**

Dimensions of the cuboid = 10 cm, 8 cm, 6 cm.

A cube of maximum possible size is cut from one corner.

**Formulas Used:**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid = 2 × (lb + bh + hl)

Area lost from corner cut = 3 × a²

Area created inside the cut = 3 × a²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Maximum side of the cube that can be cut = minimum(10, 8, 6) = 6 cm.

⇒ When a cube is cut from a corner, exactly 3 outer faces are removed.

⇒ At the same time, 3 identical inner faces are newly exposed to balance it out.

⇒ Net change in Total Surface Area = (Added Area) − (Lost Area) = (3 × a²) − (3 × a²) = 0.

⇒ Therefore, the TSA of the remaining solid remains unchanged.

⇒ New TSA = Original TSA = 2 × (10 × 8 + 8 × 6 + 6 × 10)

⇒ New TSA = 2 × (80 + 48 + 60)

⇒ New TSA = 2 × 188 = 376 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 376 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

1. Surface Area Change based on Cut Position

• **Corner Cut:** TSA remains unchanged (3 faces lost, 3 faces gained).
• **Edge Cut (Middle):** TSA increases by 2 × a² (2 faces lost, 4 faces gained).
• **Face Cut (Middle):** TSA increases by 4 × a² (1 face lost, 5 faces gained).

2. Volume Change after Cutting

Unlike surface area, the volume of a solid strictly decreases when a piece is removed. The new volume is always the original volume minus the volume of the removed piece.

3. Maximum Size of the Cut Cube

The side of the largest possible cube that can be completely cut out from a given cuboid is equal to the smallest dimension among its length, breadth, and height.
